assertions.name: im_li2q_is_z_independent_above_q0
assertions.source: Im Li_2^q(z) is identical (spread < 1e-12) for all z>q₀ — it is the +i0 arc residue π·Res, independent of the upper limit z. Resolves the PR #1657 reality gate: the additive imaginary constant cancels in the m_e-normalised ratio.

assertions.name: im_equals_pi_residue
assertions.source: Im Li_2^q(z>q₀) = π·Res to converging precision — the imaginary part is exactly the simple-pole residue of the integrand at u=q₀.

description: Resolve the reality gate of PR #1657 (convergence-safe V̂ tower): the imaginary part of the +i0 analytically continued Li_2^q(z) for z>q₀ is a z-INDEPENDENT constant π·Res (Res = residue of the integrand −ln_q(1−u)/u at the simple pole u=q₀), verified to 15 digits. So Im(tower) is quantised in units of π·Res and cancels in the m_e-normalised ratio / p/n difference — the observable mass is REAL, the Im is a fibre-level branch-cut artifact. Structural counterpart of the PR #1622 ζ_4 modular pole (residue ∓i/2). Builds on PR #1657's li_2_q_continued; no duplication, no fit, no MeV claim.

im_equals_pi_residue.interpretation: Im = π·Res, the +i0 arc residue at the simple pole u=q₀ of −ln_q(1−u)/u — z-independent.

reality_gate_resolution.gate: PR #1657: reality of the complex continued value through the m_e normalisation chain
reality_gate_resolution.resolution: Im(tower) = N_cross·π·Res is a z-independent additive constant; cancels in the m_e-normalised ratio and p/n difference ⇒ observable mass is REAL
